persona.background: Plumber's daughter, two older brothers. Transistor radio tuned to 3XY and 3UZ, Countdown on ABC every Sunday night (in colour from March 1975), Go-Set and TV Week, singles bought at Brashs, blue-light and school socials.

Various Artists - Tribal Music of Australia (album)

AU1975A.wouldSay: Skyhooks! Horror Movie was on Countdown every week, Molly nearly wore it out. And Eagle Rock at every school social.
missing: The Ted Mulry Gang - Jump in My Car (1975)
Skyhooks - Ego Is Not a Dirty Word (1975)
AU1975A.fake: The opening is right, but the back half drifts into a 1953 Folkways field-recording album nobody my age played and a 1966 Kinks song, and Long Way to the Top was really a 1976 hit (the Countdown truck clip), so it reads a little like hindsight.

persona.name: Karim
persona.background: Son of an SNTF railway worker, five siblings. Raï cassettes bought from stalls at Medina Jdida and played on the family radio-cassette, weddings with live raï, RTA Chaîne 3 and Radio Oran, Egyptian films on RTA TV with his mother, Qur'an recitation at home on Fridays, older sister listened to Barbara and French radio.

Abdul Basit Abdul Samad - Surat Maryam
Abdel Halim Hafez - Zay El Hawa

DZ1985A.wouldSay: N'sel fik! That cassette was in every taxi in Oran. And Trig el Lycée, Khaled when he was still a kid, then Rimitti, my uncle would turn that one down when we were in the room.
DZ1985A.fake: Nothing rings false in the opening; the later Algiers chaabi and Kabyle picks are real but lean toward what an anthology would choose rather than what an Oran teenager played, and Dahmane El Harrachi's Ya Rayah, which everyone knew, is absent.

persona.name: Gábor
persona.background: Father a lathe operator at DIGÉP, mother a nurse. Petőfi Rádió (Csúcsforgalom, Poptarisznya), Magyar Televízió's pop shows, Pepita/Hungaroton LPs and dubbed cassettes from older cousins, school discos and KISZ camp dances, Edda as the hometown band, Radio Luxembourg at night for Western hits.

seeds.song: Tears for Fears - Everybody Wants to Rule the World

HU1985A.wouldSay: This is just Western radio. Maiden played the Budapest Sportcsarnok in '84, sure, but where is anything Hungarian? We didn't dance to Sister Sledge, we danced to R-GO.
missing: R-GO - Szeretlek is meg nem is (1983)
HU1985A.fake: Every seed is foreign, and these are UK/US chart picks rather than what Hungarian radio and school discos actually played in 1985 (Modern Talking, Opus, Italo); with zero Hungarian songs it could be any country.
